cards.front: Who was the first person to advocate the idea of an elected Constituent Assembly for India, and in which year?
cards.back: M.N. Roy in 1934. The Indian National Congress officially demanded it for the first time in 1935.
cards.key_fact: M.N. Roy proposed Constituent Assembly in 1934; INC officially demanded it in 1935.

cards.front: Which British declaration accepted for the first time the demand for a Constituent Assembly consisting 'mainly of Indians'?
cards.back: The 'August Offer' of 1940, announced by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow.
cards.key_fact: August Offer 1940 first conceded the principle of an Indian Constituent Assembly.

cards.front: Who were the three members of the Cabinet Mission that arrived in India in March 1946?
cards.back:
1. Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India)
2. Sir Stafford Cripps (President of Board of Trade)
3. A.V. Alexander (First Lord of Admiralty)
cards.key_fact: Cabinet Mission 1946 members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander.

cards.front: What was the total initial strength of the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan, and how were seats divided?
cards.back: 389 total seats: 296 seats for British India (292 from Governors' provinces + 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces) and 93 seats for Princely States.
cards.key_fact: Cabinet Mission Plan strength was 389 (296 British India + 93 Princely States).

cards.front: How were the members of the Constituent Assembly from British Indian provinces elected?
cards.back: Indirectly elected by the members of the Provincial Legislative Assemblies using the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system of proportional representation.
cards.key_fact: Assembly was partly indirectly elected (provinces) and partly nominated (princely states).

cards.front: To what number was the membership of the Constituent Assembly reduced following the partition of India under the Mountbatten Plan?
cards.back: 299 members (229 representing British Indian provinces and 70 representing Princely States).
cards.key_fact: Post-partition strength fell from 389 to 299 (229 provinces + 70 princely states).

cards.front: Who was elected as the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly on December 9, 1946, and following which convention?
cards.back: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, following the French practice of appointing the oldest member as temporary chairman.
cards.key_fact: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary Chairman on Dec 9, 1946 (French practice).

cards.front: Who were elected as the permanent President and the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946?
cards.back:
President: Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
Two Vice-Presidents: Dr. H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.
cards.key_fact: Assembly had one President (Dr. Rajendra Prasad) and two Vice-Presidents (H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari).

cards.front: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
cards.back: Sir B.N. Rau (Benegal Narsing Rau), who prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.
cards.key_fact: Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly.

cards.front: When was the historic 'Objectives Resolution' moved and adopted in the Constituent Assembly?
cards.back: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946; unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947.
cards.key_fact: Objectives Resolution moved Dec 13, 1946; adopted Jan 22, 1947 (became Preamble).

cards.front: When was the Drafting Committee appointed, and who was its Chairman?
cards.back: Appointed on August 29, 1947, consisting of 7 members under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
cards.key_fact: Drafting Committee was appointed on August 29, 1947 under Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

cards.front: Which two members of the Drafting Committee were replaced, and by whom?
cards.back:
1. N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter (who resigned due to ill health).
2. T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (who died in 1948).
cards.key_fact: Replacements: N. Madhava Rau for B.L. Mitter; T.T. Krishnamachari for D.P. Khaitan.

cards.front: Who was the Chairman of the States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States) in the Constituent Assembly?
cards.back: Jawaharlal Nehru. (Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and Advisory Committee).
cards.key_fact: States Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, NOT Sardar Patel.

cards.front: Who chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas, and who chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee?
cards.back:
Main Advisory Committee: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee: J.B. Kripalani.
Minorities Sub-Committee: H.C. Mukherjee.
cards.key_fact: Patel chaired main Advisory Committee; J.B. Kripalani chaired Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee.

cards.front: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to complete the Constitution, and how many sessions were held?
cards.back: 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days across 11 sessions (spending 114 days on the draft constitution, at a cost of approximately Rs. 64 lakh).
cards.key_fact: Total duration: 2 years, 11 months, 18 days; 11 sessions; Rs. 64 lakh total expenditure.

cards.front: What did the original Indian Constitution contain when adopted on November 26, 1949?
cards.back: A Preamble, 395 Articles (arranged into 22 Parts), and 8 Schedules.
cards.key_fact: Adopted Nov 26, 1949: Preamble + 395 Articles + 22 Parts + 8 Schedules.

cards.front: Which constitutional provision brought Citizenship and Election provisions into force immediately on November 26, 1949?
cards.back: Article 394 enforced Articles 5-9 (Citizenship), 60 (Presidential Oath), 324 (Elections), 366, 367, 379-380, 388, and 391-393 on Nov 26, 1949.
cards.key_fact: Article 394 enacted citizenship (5-9) and elections (324) immediately on Nov 26, 1949.

cards.front: Why was January 26 specifically selected as the Date of Commencement of the Indian Constitution?
cards.back: To commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence Day) celebrated on January 26, 1930 pursuant to the 1929 Lahore Congress resolution.
cards.key_fact: Jan 26 was chosen to commemorate Purna Swaraj Day (Jan 26, 1930).

cards.front: What animal was adopted as the official seal (symbol) of the Constituent Assembly?
cards.back: The Elephant.
cards.key_fact: The official symbol and seal of the Constituent Assembly was the Elephant.

cards.front: Who was the calligrapher of the original handwritten English Constitution, and which artists illuminated it?
cards.back:
Calligrapher: Prem Behari Narain Raizada (in flowing italic style).
Illuminators: Shantiniketan artists under Acharya Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha.
cards.key_fact: Raizada was the English calligrapher; Nand Lal Bose and Rammanohar Sinha illuminated it.
